text: yeah the current V* system has some conflicts because its all an ongoing learning experience of what does and doesnt work out well; alright so with that being said can you make a parity and if then you need some mock data to compare just generate a huge world that both can compile data from and compare side by side
resolution: Added a repeatable TS/Zig compiler parity harness for the hmsc compiled-route data format. The new rjit game parity command writes one deterministic generated-world source spec, compiles it through the existing TypeScript workspace writer and a new Zig RJMP/gamefile writer/compiler, byte-compares the emitted gamefiles, and reports side-by-side timings. This deliberately targets the platform-format compiler core first: row-RLE, lump container layout, three game streams, sha256 asset manifest, and embedded blobs; live editor store readers and full asset cookers remain the next migration layer.
